before:
Spoken assistance can help a user connect an instruction with an object in an immersive environment, but the choice of guiding voice presents a separate design question. Would guidance feel or function differently if it sounded like the person receiving it? Follow My Voice investigates self-similar synthetic speech in comparison with a catalog voice the participant has chosen to hear. This comparison asks whether resemblance offers a different form of assistance from an already preferred voice, considering both search efficiency and participant experience.

The proposed within-participant study comprises one practice trial in the first assigned voice followed by two counterbalanced blocks of 40 measured trials. In a seated mixed-reality search task, target identity is withheld and spoken directions guide participants toward objects distributed across eight surrounding vertical planes. Both voices use the same gaze-contingent guidance policy, phrase library, and right-controller selection method. Gaze tracking and constrained agent decisions provide a shared delivery mechanism for the voice comparison; they are not separate experimental factors.

The primary analysis will compare active completion time between self-similar and preferred catalog voices while accounting for starting geometry and participant clustering. Perceived voice similarity will be checked separately from performance. Workload, motivation, and agent experience will be assessed retrospectively after both blocks, with condition-specific ratings referenced to their corresponding block; debriefing will explore reactions to hearing the self-similar voice and possible uses for it. The system records actual voice exposure and guidance delivery to help distinguish a voice-condition difference from a technical delivery problem. This first pass develops the rationale, study design, supporting apparatus, and analysis plan. Confirmatory participant outcomes are not yet available, so no performance advantage or preference for self-similar voice is claimed.
after:
Directing users' attention to objects of interest has long been a concern in virtual reality, particularly when relevant objects lie outside the user's current field of view~\cite{grogorick2017subtle,lange2020hivefive}. Research in augmented reality has shown that auditory guidance, including verbal hints, can support object search~\cite{zhang2023seehear}. Spoken assistance can connect spatial instructions with objects in the surrounding environment, guiding users toward a region and then the intended object. Yet the guiding voice may also shape how users respond to assistance. This thesis compares guidance spoken in a synthetic voice resembling the participant's own with guidance spoken in a participant-selected, non-self-similar catalog voice.

Follow My Voice will investigate this comparison in a within-participant mixed-reality user study. Participants will complete one practice trial in their first assigned voice and two counterbalanced blocks of 40 measured trials. Seated participants will search colored geometric objects on eight surrounding vertical planes, including locations initially outside their field of view. The participant will not be told the target's identity; instead, gaze-contingent spoken directions will guide orientation toward its region and progressively refine the search. Participants will select the inferred target using the right-controller ray and trigger. Both conditions will use the same guidance policy and phrase library to focus the comparison on voice.

The study will compare active search-completion time, perceived workload, motivation, and agent experience. Voice-similarity ratings and debriefing will examine whether participants recognize the resemblance and how they perceive receiving guidance in their own synthetic voice. Condition-specific questionnaires will be administered after both blocks. This thesis presents the apparatus and study plan; participant results are not yet available.
scope: Abstract only; study remains proposed and comparator remains participant-selected catalog voice.
